name: Bank of Baroda
title: Bank of Baroda - 532134 - Transcript Of Media Meet And Analyst Meet Q2 Results

summary.headline: Bank of Baroda Q2 FY27 net profit hit record INR 6,532 crore (+35.8% YoY) helped by INR 1,349 crore NSE sale gain; guidance upsized to 13-15% credit growth.
summary.overview: Global business crossed INR 32 lakh crore (INR 32.58 lakh crore, +17.2% YoY), with global advances up 18.3% and deposits up 16.4%, both helped by the FCNR(B) scheme (about USD 8.08 billion raised). Management said growth excluding FCNR(B) was 13.5% for advances and 11.2% for deposits. Operating profit was a record INR 11,430 crore, but included a one-off NSE gain; excluding the NSE impact it was INR 7,749 crore. The bank also made about INR 1,600 crore of extra provisions (INR 1,300 crore prudential on NPAs and INR 300 crore contingency) as an ECL buffer, so credit cost was 55 bps against 18 bps excluding it. Full-year credit and deposit growth guidance was raised by 1 percentage point.

financial_highlights.change: +50.9% YoY; includes NSE one-off; INR 7,749 crore excluding NSE impact
ROA +19 bps YoY; ROE +363 bps YoY
GNPA -38 bps YoY; NNPA -20 bps YoY
CD ratio down 323 bps YoY; CASA ex-FCNR(B) above 38%
Fell sharply YoY and QoQ, helped by NSE gain

segments.name: Retail and Agri
segments.commentary: Organic retail grew 18.6% YoY and agri 19%; auto loans +27.8%, mortgage +20.3%, home loans +14.6%, education +9.9%, personal loans +6.8%. Retail gold declined YTD, while agri gold grows about 8% QoQ.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Organic MSME book grew 21.3% YoY, which management said is slightly above 20% for several quarters, supported by government guarantee schemes.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate loans grew 6.3% YoY (about 15.3% in June). Mid-corporate grew about 26% and core corporate about 12%; the decline is in fine-priced high-quality assets where the bank is refusing to cut pricing.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: International advances grew 39.7% YoY; international deposits grew 14.9% YoY.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Total deposits +16.4% YoY; domestic CASA +10.4% YoY and term deposits +20.5% YoY. Retail deposits ex-FCNR(B) grew about 8.3% and bulk deposits about 14.5%.

segments.name: Subsidiaries and new entities
segments.commentary: Card subsidiary is described as the fourth-largest by net acquisition this year. BOB Securities, Giltedge (PD, DCM, pension fund) were launched. Management did not disclose card issuance or book size.

guidance_outlook: Full-year credit growth guidance raised to 13-15% from 12-14%.
Full-year deposit growth guidance raised to 11-13% from 10-12%.
NIM guidance held at 2.75-2.95%, with management expecting an upward bias in Q3 and Q4 as about 38% of the book is repo-linked and repo was raised on 5 October.
Credit cost guided below 0.6%; slippage ratio guided at 1-1.25%.
ROA expected above 1% in Q3 and Q4; full-year ROA targeted near 1%. ROE guidance 15-16%.
Recovery from TWO run rate about INR 750 crore average, expected to be met in Q3 and Q4; harder beyond FY27. Fee income seen improving over the next two quarters as the fee structure is reviewed.
capex_capacity: ECL migration: one-time CRAR impact estimated around 125 bps (about INR 12,500 crore); about INR 2,500 crore floating provision already held. Recurring credit cost could rise to 30-35 bps gross or 20-25 bps net.
IT spend at about 10% of operating profit, with a stated ceiling of 15%; bank is hiring heavily in IT.
BOB World 2.0 app went live this quarter, with AI features, voice banking and a personal finance manager.
CRR at 99% impact about INR 2,000-3,000 crore, according to management.
Pipeline of over INR 60,000 crore (under processing or sanctioned-not-disbursed) in corporate.
demand_pricing: FCNR(B) inflow of about USD 8.08 billion; about INR 74,000-75,000 crore converted to rupees is held as 'stored liquidity' for Dec and March busy-season funding. Bulk deposits were cut only about INR 10,000 crore so far.

Management said about 70% of FCNR(B) funds are linked to overseas leveraged loans; annual interest outgo estimated at USD 350-400 million at 6.5-6.75%, with the remaining unhedged portion under review for hedging.
Corporate pricing discipline: the bank is declining to match lower pricing on high-quality corporate assets, which is holding back corporate growth.
Rising repo and sub-MCLR repricing are expected to lift margins; cost of deposits 4.71% in the quarter, up slightly.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the NSE and valuation gain was taken into profit, and how much of it was used for provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Total NSE effect is about INR 3,600 crore, made up of about INR 1,300-1,349 crore cash profit and the rest valuation gain. About INR 1,600 crore of this was put into prudential and contingency provisions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 1,300 crore prudential provision for ECL?
qa_highlights.answer: It is specific provisioning on NPA and bad-debt accounts, not standard-asset provisioning. The INR 300 crore contingency sits in other provisions to cover bond and equity valuation swings. The CFO declined to give a standard-asset ECL estimate, saying the bank is still computing it.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FCNR(B) money being used to repay bulk deposits or to fund loans?
qa_highlights.answer: It is stored liquidity. Only about INR 10,000 crore of bulk deposits were reduced. The funds will go to repay high-cost bulk deposits if rates stay elevated, or otherwise to credit growth. Management says the net book impact is the same either way.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 13-15% credit guidance achievable given the first-half run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: The RAM book is expected to add about INR 60,000 crore, and the corporate pipeline is more than INR 60,000 crore. Management says this is achievable, as the same period in Q3 and Q4 last year delivered a similar increase.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the 99% CRR requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: The impact is estimated at INR 2,000-3,000 crore, which management does not regard as significant.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bank considering ECB or ODI borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: The bank has raised USD 1.1 billion against a USD 4 billion mandate, valid until December. It will tap more only if pricing is right.

risks_watch: Quality of earnings: about INR 3,600 crore NSE effect, of which INR 1,600 crore was reinvested as provisions. Excluding it, operating profit is about INR 7,749 crore, so Q3 earnings will reveal the run rate.
ECL transition: one-time CRAR hit of about 125 bps and recurring credit cost rise of 20-35 bps. Standard-asset provisioning under ECL has not been disclosed.
FCNR(B) unhedged currency exposure and interest outgo of USD 350-400 million a year, with hedging decisions pending.
Cyber and data security: a data leak was reported, and management says the exposed data was largely unusable or already public. Forensic audit and security revamp are under way.
Rising rates, drought/El Nino effects on agri and restructuring under SLBC guidance (no state schemes yet), and gold loan scrutiny.
Insurance commission rules and MDR deferral; management could not quantify the impact on distribution income.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability, with the balance sheet described as strong and asset quality as pristine. Cautious and evasive on specifics: it declined to give standard-asset ECL numbers, gave no card book size, and deferred the MTM and FCNR fee-income answers.
key_quotes: So, as against 12 to 14%, we are now projecting at 13 to 15%.
This is the highest ever operating profit posted by the Bank.
The credit cost without the prudential provision would have been 18 bps.

growth.why: Full-year credit growth guidance raised to 13-15% (midpoint 14%) and deposit guidance to 11-13%, backed by a INR 60,000 crore+ corporate pipeline and retail/MSME momentum, but no physical capacity additions were disclosed and the FCNR(B)-inflated growth flatters the headline.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM guided 2.75-2.95% with upward bias in Q3 and Q4 as about 38% of the book is repo-linked and repo was raised on 5 October; Q2 NIM was 2.74%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Credit growth guidance raised to 13-15% (from 12-14%) and deposits to 11-13%, backed by a INR 60,000 crore+ corporate pipeline and RAM book expected to add about INR 60,000 crore; ex-FCNR(B) advances growth was 13.5%.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Credit and deposit guidance were already raised by 1 pp and ROA is guided above 1% for Q3-Q4, but management kept NIM, credit cost and ROE guidance unchanged.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: ECL migration could cost about 125 bps of CRAR (about INR 12,500 crore) and lift recurring credit cost to 30-35 bps gross; credit cost guided below 0.6% and Q2 was 0.55% including provisions, and the NSE gain of INR 7,749 crore excluded makes the run rate harder.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: BOB World 2.0 with AI features went live this quarter and the card subsidiary is active, but no card book size or new product timing was disclosed.

rows.label: Corporate pipeline above INR 60,000 crore
rows.why: Pipeline of over INR 60,000 crore (under processing or sanctioned-not-disbursed) is cited as the basis for achieving the 13-15% credit guidance, with mid-corporate growing about 26%.

rows.label: FCNR(B) repayment of high-cost bulk deposits
rows.why: About INR 74,000-75,000 crore of FCNR(B) funds held as stored liquidity; only about INR 10,000 crore of bulk deposits cut so far, with repayment depending on whether rates stay elevated.

rows.label: CRR at 99% drag of INR 2,000-3,000 crore
rows.why: Management estimates a CRR impact of INR 2,000-3,000 crore and does not regard it as significant.

tone.note: Management was confident on credit growth, ROA and asset quality, but cautious and evasive on standard-asset ECL numbers, card book size and FCNR fee income; analysts pressed on the NSE gain used for provisions and the achievability of 13-15% growth given the first-half run rate.
